true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition above it. Existing calls passing width, height, and options now raise ArgumentError; calls passing just width and height treat the height as `opts` and fail when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both call forms in a single method or give the dimensions-based method a separate name so existing image-downsizing callers continue to work.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Keep the configured size limit for non-image attachments

The unconditional 10 MB limit also applies to attachments, although the new server-side downsizing applies only to images. This removes enforcement of `max_attachment_size_kb` in the client: attachments above a smaller configured limit are submitted only to be rejected by the server, while attachments allowed by a configured limit above 10 MB can no longer be uploaded through the UI. Apply the expanded input limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Oversized animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when it is allowed

The downsizing call passes the multipart tempfile path, which normally has no `.gif` extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects its animated implementation only when the input path ends in `.GIF`, so `allow_animation: true` does not preserve animation here. The regular conversion reads only `from[0]` and overwrites the uploaded file with its first frame. Consequently, uploading an oversized animated GIF permanently discards its animation despite `allow_animated_thumbnails` being enabled. Detect the format independently of the temporary filename or use an appropriately suffixed working file.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize existing hosts before inserting them

The migration copies host strings directly into the table, bypassing the new model's scheme/path normalization. The previous implementation explicitly accepted entries such as `https://eviltrout.com`, but the new lookup compares the stored value with only `URI(url).host`. Such migrated entries will never match, so existing embeds stop working after upgrading, and the original setting is then deleted. Normalize migrated hosts using the same rules as newly created records.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration fails when no embed category is configured

The category query is indexed with `[0]['id']` before checking whether it returned a row. When `embed_category` is unset, blank, or names a deleted category, the join returns no rows and accessing row zero raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents ordinary installations that have never configured embedding from upgrading. Check for an empty result before reading the ID, and handle a missing uncategorized setting row as well.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Accepted hosts containing ports never match requests

The validator accepts values such as `example.com:8080`, and normalization leaves the port intact, but `record_for_host` extracts only `uri.host`, which is `example.com`. Consequently, a successfully saved host with a port never authorizes embedding and never supplies its category during import. Make storage and lookup consistent about ports, or reject port-bearing entries rather than saving unusable configuration.

Duplicate hosts make category mappings ambiguous

There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for hosts, so the editor can save the same hostname more than once with different categories. Imports select only the first matching record, ignoring the other mappings; editing a later duplicate can therefore appear successful while having no effect on where topics are posted. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname so each host has one unambiguous category mapping.

Valid domains with longer top-level names cannot be configured

The host validator limits the final domain label to two through five letters. Valid domains such as `example.museum` and `example.technology` therefore cannot be added or saved in the embedding editor, even though they are usable HTTP hosts. Use domain validation that supports current top-level domains rather than imposing this length limit.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle users without an existing topic-user record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally reads its notification_level. Although sending a notification email creates a record for its recipient, the unsubscribe URL is not bound to that recipient: someone opening a forwarded email while logged into another account, or opening the URL before interacting with the topic, may have no record. The endpoint then returns a server error instead of unsubscribing. Treat a missing record as the default notification level and create it through TopicUser.change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification preferences through an unauthenticated GET action

The new GET route immediately changes the logged-in user's notification level, using only the session cookie and a predictable topic URL. GET requests do not receive Rails' normal CSRF-token protection, and this action also skips the XHR check. An external site can therefore cause a logged-in visitor to unsubscribe from a topic by navigating them to this URL, without their consent. Serve the confirmation page on GET and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST, or use an appropriately scoped signed unsubscribe token.

Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed and records notifications_changed_at. For a topic-user record whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read can subsequently overwrite the unsubscribed regular or muted level with tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached. Thus reading the topic after unsubscribing can undo the choice automatically. Apply the new level through the existing preference-change API so the explicit choice is preserved.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent matches lose counter increments

The match counter is updated by reading a record, incrementing its in-memory value, and saving it without locking. Two concurrent requests matching the same blocked address can both read a count of N and both save N+1, recording only one of the two matches. Use an atomic database increment or lock the record while updating the statistics to keep match_count accurate under concurrent signup attempts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email blocks can be bypassed by changing address casing

The blocked-email lookup uses case-sensitive equality, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes the address before this lookup. For example, blocking `block@spamfromhome.org` still allows signup with `block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG`, which identifies the same mailbox because domain names are case-insensitive. Normalize stored blocked addresses and lookup values consistently with the application's email handling so casing cannot bypass a block.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB Ruby prevents existing discussions from rendering

The opening `if` is closed with `end if`, leaving a trailing `if` without a condition. Rails cannot compile this template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. Close the block with `end`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle RSS entries that use description or content:encoded

The poller assumes every item has a non-nil `content` field. Ordinary RSS feeds commonly provide the body through `description` or `content:encoded` instead, so `i.content.scrub` raises for those entries. This aborts the entire polling run, preventing the entry and all subsequent entries from importing. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle missing bodies explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Resolve relative URLs with URI joining instead of prefix concatenation

The URL rewriting handles only values starting with `/` and treats protocol-relative URLs as local paths. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, while `images/photo.jpg` remains relative to the forum rather than the source article. The same problem affects links. Resolve references against the source URL with URI joining so imported images and links continue to point to their original destinations.

Sanitize imported HTML before storing it as cooked content

Feed content reaches this method without HTML sanitization, and the post is created with `raw_html`, which makes `Post#cook` return the HTML unchanged. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or dangerous URL schemes. Consequently, malicious HTML in a feed becomes stored executable content on the forum's origin. Sanitize both initial imports and revisions before bypassing the normal cooking pipeline.

Validate redirect destinations before fetching embedded pages

The request-driven retrieval path checks only the hostname of the original embed URL, then uses `open(url)`, which follows HTTP redirects. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host can therefore make the worker fetch internal services or attacker-controlled content despite the hostname restriction. Validate the scheme, port, resolved address, and each redirect destination before fetching rather than relying solely on the initial host check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name

The new website_name attribute is not included in untrusted_attributes, and include_website_name lacks the trailing `?` required for a serializer inclusion predicate. Consequently, anonymous requests for TL0 profiles receive the website hostname (and, for matching domains, its path) even when scope.restrict_user_fields? suppresses website itself. The updated template also displays that restricted information. Add website_name to the same visibility guard as website and use a correctly named inclusion predicate.

false_positives.candidate:
Refresh the website label when saving profile changes

The label now comes from the server-populated website_name instead of a computed property dependent on model.website. User.save() sends the changed website but only copies bio_excerpt from the response; it never updates website_name. After changing or clearing a website on the loaded user model, the profile can therefore show the old domain with a new or empty link target, or keep a newly added website hidden, until user details are fetched again. Update website_name from the save response or otherwise recompute it when website changes.

Preserve the light-theme color for embedded-post author links

Retain the existing light-theme topic-map heading color

The new light-theme branch changes topic-map h3 headings from a 20% primary lightness adjustment to 50%. Update notification-badge text when darkening its background

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

Exact multiples of the page size produce an extra empty page

totalPages uses floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which overcounts whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the limit. For example, a 50-member group with limit 50 displays two pages and enables Next; clicking it requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use ceiling division for the number of pages.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Existing membership PATCH requests now silently change group visibility

The previous update action supported PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes.add and changes.delete, as demonstrated by the removed incremental-update tests. The route still accepts PATCH, but this action now ignores changes and unconditionally sets visible to false when no visible parameter is supplied. Existing clients therefore receive a successful response without the requested membership change, while also unexpectedly hiding the group. Preserve the PATCH contract or explicitly reject unsupported requests without modifying the group.

Public group member lists are truncated with no way to fetch subsequent pages

The public members route now calls findMembers() with its default limit of 50, and the server applies that limit to every group. However, the public members template has no pagination controls or load-more behavior. A custom group with more than 50 members, which previously displayed all members, now permanently hides everyone after the first 50. Add pagination to the public page or preserve its complete member listing.

Removing the final member on a page leaves pagination at an invalid offset

removeMember reloads members using the existing offset without moving back when the current page becomes empty. For example, removing the only member on page 3 of a 101-member group leaves offset 100 after the total falls to 100. Subsequent reloads still return an empty list because findMembers clamps the offset to the member count rather than to the start of the last valid page. Normalize the offset to a valid page after membership removal so the administrator sees the remaining members.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Include the site fallback locale in the translation cache key

The new fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the translation cache key contains only the requested key, current locale, and backend identity. If the site default changes—or sites with different defaults share this process—a cached translation missing from the user's locale is reused even though it should now resolve through a different site locale. Loading the new fallback locale does not invalidate this cached result. Include the fallback configuration or site identity in the cache key, or invalidate the cache whenever that configuration changes.

Load fallback locales for translations outside controller requests

Fallback translations are preloaded only by ApplicationController#set_locale. The translation accelerator still loads only the current locale, and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks searches other locales directly through the backend without invoking that loader. In a fresh worker or other non-controller context, a missing non-English translation therefore cannot fall back to English (or the site locale) because those YAML files have not been loaded. Ensure the fallback chain is loaded on the translation path itself rather than relying on a controller filter.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the user to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled

This calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the method added to UsernamePasswordForm requires a UserModel argument. There is no zero-argument overload in the supplied hierarchy, so UsernameForm does not compile and the services module cannot build. Pass context.getUser() to the helper.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Keep conditional passkeys enabled before a user is identified

The new helper requires user != null, but ordinary login starts with context.getUser() == null. Both authenticate() and the error challenge now use this helper, so they no longer call fillContextForm() during ordinary username/password or username-only login. Consequently, the initial page lacks the conditional WebAuthn UI and challenge, breaking discoverable-passkey login and the existing tests that expect passkeys before entering a username. The predicate must support unidentified users as well as re-authentication.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Django querysets do not support negative slicing

When advanced features are enabled and the cursor offset is negative, this branch passes a negative slice start to a Django QuerySet. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing with ValueError rather than handling boundary conditions automatically. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature produces a server error, even with cursor value zero, before any rows are retrieved. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or translate them into a supported query instead of slicing with a negative index.

true_positives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle organization contexts without a member

Organization-authenticated API requests can have organization_context.member=None, such as requests authorized through an organization API token. This new expression unconditionally dereferences that member whenever request.user.is_superuser is false, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Such requests previously used the normal paginator but now fail with AttributeError. Only evaluate advanced authorization when requested, and explicitly handle contexts without a member.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs

The audit-log endpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so building cursors for any nonempty optimized page raises TypeError and returns a server error. value_from_cursor also returns a number instead of converting the timestamp back to a datetime. Reuse DateTimePaginator's conversions (or inherit from it) so both initial requests and subsequent cursor requests work.

Django raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") rather than handling the boundary automatically. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature produces a server error on the optimized audit-log endpoint. The optimized audit-log paginator cannot handle datetime keys

OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. Consequently, an authorized user's optimized_pagination=true request fails whenever results are nonempty. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value instead of converting it to a datetime. false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Changing existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets requires a migration

The buffer now uses ZADD and ZSCAN on the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous version populated with SADD. Any buffered segment present during deployment remains a Redis set, so new insertions and flushing those segments fail with WRONGTYPE. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read or write each other's buffers. Provide a compatible conversion or a versioned-key rollout that drains the old buffers before switching; otherwise deployment stalls processing of existing data.

Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit

SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the Python span-count check was removed and this script unconditionally caps every segment at 1000. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments exceeding that limit, while a larger configured limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit to the insertion script and use it for eviction, or explicitly remove the configurable contract rather than leaving it ineffective.

Unioning sorted sets must preserve timestamps rather than sum them

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. A replayed span can exist both in the destination buffer and in a newly staged parent buffer when that parent has already been redirected. Merging those buffers doubles the duplicate payload's end-timestamp score, although its actual timestamp has not changed. Subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction then retains these replayed old spans ahead of genuinely newer spans. Use an aggregation mode such as MAX so merging duplicate payloads preserves their timestamp.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check upsampling against the dataset actually being queried

The eligibility check uses the outer `dataset`, while query execution uses `scoped_dataset`. These differ in the dashboard splitting paths: a metrics-enhanced request can execute an error-only query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and rejects upsampling. As a result, sampled error charts produced by those paths continue to report stored counts rather than estimated counts. Pass the actual scoped dataset and effective query into the eligibility check.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Apply weighted counting to top-event selection as well as its time series

For top-events requests, only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to weighted counting; `selected_columns` and `orderby` are still passed directly from the original request. A request selecting and ordering by `count()` therefore chooses its top groups using stored-event counts, then plots weighted counts for those groups. With differing client sample rates, a group with fewer stored events can have the largest estimated count and still be excluded from the chart. Transform the selection and ranking aggregates consistently with the time-series aggregate.

Parse the query instead of using a substring to identify error-only searches

The presence of `event.type:error` does not mean a Discover query selects only errors. For example, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` both pass this check. For allowlisted projects, their count is then replaced with an aggregation over `sample_weight`, even though the helper explicitly states that transactions do not have that field. These valid searches can consequently fail or return incorrect counts. Determine whether the parsed query actually restricts results to errors before applying the transformation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New table visualization discards the widget's query results

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the chart passes empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata to TableWidgetVisualization instead of the actual `result`. Every dashboard table widget in an enabled organization therefore renders empty even when its query returned rows. Pass the real results and configured columns into the new visualization before enabling this branch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Attribute query cache is not scoped to the organization

The new query key contains only the query options, while the query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Two organizations with the same project selection (for example, all projects), date range, item type, and attribute type share a cache entry. Switching organizations can therefore display custom attribute names fetched from the previous organization, and concurrent consumers can reuse the wrong organization's results. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the query key.

Normalize error and recording timestamps before merging

Error timestamps read from nodestore are Unix seconds, but recording events use rrweb timestamps in Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly causes essentially every error to be emitted before the first recording event, regardless of when it actually occurred. The new tests use seconds for recording timestamps and consequently miss this production behavior. Convert recording timestamps to seconds, or error timestamps to milliseconds, before performing the chronological merge.

Respect falsy results from custom cell renderers

Both custom renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` to decide whether to accept the custom result, although the documented contract says only `undefined` invokes the fallback. Valid React results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null` are therefore replaced by the default renderer. This prevents callers from intentionally rendering zero or suppressing a cell's contents. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both the header and body wrappers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is not atomic

The backup-code list is read before validation and then overwritten with an update conditioned only on the user ID. Two concurrent login requests can read the same list, validate the same code, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, making a consumed code usable again. Consume codes atomically, such as through a conditional update against the previously read ciphertext whose success is checked before granting access.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
A dummy TOTP value lets backup-code login bypass the password

Password verification above this branch runs only when credentials.totpCode is empty. A caller can therefore submit an account's email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode (for example, "x") without supplying the password. This new branch accepts the backup code and never validates the supplied TOTP, so authentication succeeds with only the recovery code instead of both authentication factors. Ensure password authentication for CAL accounts cannot be skipped by supplying an unverified TOTP alongside a backup code.

Identity-provider users cannot access backup-code recovery

When totpEmail is present after Google or SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter. Only TwoFactorFooter exposes the Lost access button, so these users can never reach the backup-code input. This affects accounts that generated backup codes while using CAL authentication and subsequently switched to an identity provider: the authentication callbacks retain their enabled 2FA and backup codes. The server also rejects a third-party account's backup-only submission because its identity-provider guards require totpCode. Provide a recovery route for this flow and make the server accept its backup-code authentication; otherwise users with valid saved codes remain locked out after losing their authenticator.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guard the missing destination calendar before checking Google Meet

When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. For a Google Meet location, accessing its integration throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Booking creation therefore fails for event types that still select Google Meet after their destination calendar has been removed. Use optional chaining here.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Restore organization slug assignment when team billing is disabled

The condition for storing the organization slug has been inverted. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED false, organization creation now stores neither slug nor requestedSlug, even though the supplied slug is checked for collisions and used to configure the domain. Self-hosted or other non-billing deployments therefore create organizations without the slug needed to identify their organization URLs. Preserve the previous non-billing slug assignment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass each calendar adapter its own destination

Every host's credential receives the entire destinationCalendar array. Only the Google adapter selects a destination by credentialId; Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService all use the first element. Consequently, a secondary host's Office365 or Lark credential attempts to create an event in the main host's calendar, typically failing with an inaccessible or invalid calendar ID. CalDAV can filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Pass a per-destination event to these adapters or make all adapters select by credentialId.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel recurring events using each reference's credential

In the allRemainingBookings branch, the credential resolved for the current host is discarded. The code instead loops only over the booking owner's credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. With multiple collective hosts, this repeats deletion of the first host's events while never deleting the other hosts' events, despite marking every booking cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the corresponding credentialId for each deletion.

Initialize the destination array before adding collective hosts

If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently discards all destination calendars collected from the other collective hosts. Those hosts receive no calendar events even when their calendars are connected. Initialize an empty array and append the collected destinations regardless of whether the organizer has one.

Preserve credential IDs on video references

This change sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, discarding the credential ID returned by video meeting creation. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created Zoom and other dedicated video bookings will therefore leave their remote meetings active after cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video references.

Reconstruct collective destinations when confirming pending bookings

Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar with only the booking's single stored destination or the confirming user's destination. The additional collective destinations assembled in handleNewBooking are not persisted on the booking, and this handler does not reload them. Thus collective bookings requiring confirmation still create calendar events for only one host when approved. Reload the participating hosts' destinations before invoking handleConfirmation; the payment confirmation paths need the same treatment.

Retain destination selection for calendars without a credential ID

EventManager explicitly supports destination calendars without a credentialId by invoking the credentials matching their integration. This new lookup cannot match such a destination to the numeric credentialId passed to createEvent, so Google always inserts into primary rather than the configured externalId. Existing destinations using that fallback will start putting bookings in the wrong calendar. Preserve the legacy selection when the destination has no credentialId.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token

The helper inserts the literal "refresh_token" whenever the response omits refresh_token, even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365CalendarService accepts refresh responses without a new refresh token and merges parsed fields into its existing credentials; this new dummy field overwrites the valid stored refresh token. The next refresh then sends the dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The shared-response schema strips expiry and refresh-token fields

Using a Zod schema's toString() as a computed property name does not create a wildcard validator. These properties become literal keys (normally "[object Object]"), and z.object strips unrecognized fields. With credential sharing enabled, a response containing access_token, expires_in and refresh_token therefore loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom subsequently calculates an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit response fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh persists the safeParse result instead of credential data

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse wrapper { success: true, data: ... }, unlike the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call, which returned the credentials themselves. Saving this wrapper as Credential.key removes access_token and the other expected fields from the top level. After any successful refresh, including with syncing disabled, the next GoogleCalendarService construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the parsed data rather than the wrapper.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The sync branch returns a different response type from SDK refreshes

The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, but several callers expect their refresh callback's SDK-specific return value. Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of those fields, so enabling syncing causes these integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize and decode the sync response into the contract expected by each caller.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The sync branch returns a different response type from SDK refreshes

The sync branch returns an unparsed fetch Response, but several callers expect their refresh callback's SDK-specific return value. Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of those fields, so enabling syncing causes these integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize and decode the sync response into the contract expected by each caller.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not its credential ID

refreshOAuthTokens treats its third argument as a user ID and sends it as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated, so a sync endpoint will either fail to locate the account or return another user's token when the numbers happen to match. Carry credential.userId through to this call while retaining credentialId only for the database update.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using the new credential update

The new refresh path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file has no prisma import or declaration. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws ReferenceError after Salesforce successfully returns a token. Import the Prisma client used by the other integration services.

Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint

The new Salesforce refresh unconditionally posts to Salesforce rather than using refreshOAuthTokens. Thus, even with credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT configured, Cal.com independently refreshes the provider token and requires a locally stored refresh token. An external app store supplying only an access token cannot keep this integration working, and it is not the source of truth for refreshes as it is for the other integrations. Route this refresh through the sync helper.

The advertised minimal sync response is incompatible with provider parsers

The helper says the sync endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but its fetch-based callers still require provider-specific response structures. Webex validates scope, token_type, refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in; Lark requires a success code and nested data containing refresh-token expiry fields. An endpoint implementing the stated minimal contract cannot refresh either integration. Add adapters that merge the minimal response with existing credentials, or define and document the provider-specific contract actually required.

Use the installed Zoom app slug in sync requests

The refresh request sends appSlug="zoomvideo", while the Zoom OAuth callback creates credentials with appId="zoom" and the new webhook resolves applications by their actual slug. A parent app store using that same slug to look up credentials cannot resolve this refresh request. Send "zoom" consistently with the credential and webhook contracts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without lowercasing them. Zod's email validation accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a mixed-case version of a blacklisted address bypasses the blacklist and receives an invitation. Normalize incoming addresses before applying the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Authorize team administrators or owners rather than requiring both

The isTeamAdminOrOwner check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. This requires the caller to satisfy both role checks instead of either one. A team administrator who is neither the organizer nor an attendee is consequently rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. Combine the role checks with OR.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deduplicate incoming guests on the server

uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove repetitions within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct API request containing the same new address twice passes validation and sends both entries to createMany. This can create duplicate attendees and duplicate invitations despite the UI's uniqueness validation. Enforce uniqueness server-side before inserting attendees.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Respect event-type email suppression when adding guests

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee, unlike the adjacent scheduling and location-change flows that honor disableStandardEmails metadata. The handler also does not pass event-type metadata to this function. Adding a guest therefore sends standard emails even for event types whose host or attendee notifications have explicitly been disabled. Accept the metadata and apply the existing host and attendee suppression checks.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Handle seated bookings through the seat allocation flow

This mutation accepts seated bookings but inserts ordinary attendees without checking seatsPerTimeSlot or creating seat references. The new action is also exposed for these bookings. As a result, callers can add attendees beyond the configured capacity, and those attendees have no seat reference for the seat-specific cancellation and rescheduling links used by the booking UI. Either reject seated bookings in this flow or allocate guests through the seat-booking logic with capacity checks and seat references.

Reject guest additions to inactive or unconfirmed bookings

The handler checks permissions and guest addresses but never checks the booking status. An authorized caller can invoke it for a cancelled or rejected booking, after which new guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail and existing attendees receive an ICS request marked CONFIRMED. Pending bookings can likewise receive confirmed invitations without being approved. Validate that the booking is in a supported status before inserting guests or issuing calendar updates and notifications.

Update calendars using the booking organizer's credentials

The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. When the caller is not the booking organizer, those credentials do not authorize updates to the organizer's existing calendar event. Guests are already persisted before this update is attempted, so the booking can gain attendees while the actual calendar invitation remains unchanged or the mutation fails. Use the booking organizer's credentials for the calendar update.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment the retry counter atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they can both read 0 and write 1, losing one failure. The reminder then survives despite having failed twice and receives additional scheduling attempts. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than assigning a value from the stale snapshot.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch

The catch block now awaits a database update without handling errors from that update. If the reminder has been deleted while scheduling was in progress (for example, by an overlapping cron's expired-reminder cleanup), Prisma's update throws because the row no longer exists. A database outage can likewise make both the original update and this recovery update fail. That exception escapes the per-reminder catch, aborting the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed; previously the catch logged the error and continued. Handle failures of the retry-count update separately so one reminder's bookkeeping failure does not stop the batch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Migrate callers before removing the findMany API

This replaces the public `findMany(args)` method with `getBaseConditions()`, but the PR only migrates the integration test and includes no production caller updates or compatibility method. Existing callers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail TypeScript compilation (or throw `findMany is not a function` at runtime). Keep a compatible query method or migrate all consumers to execute raw queries with the new conditions in the same change.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use an in-place edit command that also works on Linux

The command `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS syntax. With GNU sed on Linux, the empty argument is treated as the script or an input filename and the command fails instead of updating an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL entry. The script does not check the exit status and still prints that the URL was updated, leaving webhook tests pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable edit strategy or select the appropriate sed syntax for the host platform.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The cache deletion success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper passes its optional external onChanged callback rather than a query refetch, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no refetching callback is supplied, successful deletion therefore leaves the old cache timestamp and deletion action visible until the page is reloaded. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on success, as the disconnect mutation already does.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellation before completing the booking cancellation

The reminder helpers now perform the database update or deletion themselves, but their returned promises are discarded by the nested forEach calls. Previously, database reminder deletions were included in the awaited Promise.all. The handler can now report a successful cancellation while its cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are still pending; in a serverless request those operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders eligible to be sent. Collect and await these helper promises, including the equivalent requestReschedule calls.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel imminent reminders without waiting for the cron job

Scheduled emails are now only marked cancelled, even when their send time is before the next 15-minute cron run. For example, an email due at 10:10 for a booking cancelled at 10:01 after the 10:00 run will still be sent. At 10:15, scheduleEmailReminders deletes the expired reminder before attempting cancellation, so it never contacts SendGrid for that email. Reminders close to their send time need an immediate cancellation path.

Do not bypass deferred cancellation for every reschedule

Passing immediateDelete=true cancels every old rescheduled-booking email immediately in SendGrid, including emails scheduled days ahead. Those cancellations remain pending until their original send dates and consume the same 100-pending-cancellation limit identified in this PR. Once that limit is reached, the helper catches the failure without setting cancelled=true, leaving the old reminder scheduled with no cron retry. Rescheduling therefore still exhausts the cancellation quota and sends obsolete reminders.

Isolate cancellation failures and persist each successful cancellation

The entire cancellation loop shares one try/catch, and its Prisma deletes are lazy promises executed only after every SendGrid request succeeds. If any request fails, all later reminders are skipped and none of the earlier successful cancellations are removed from the database. A persistent failure can consequently block unrelated cancellations on every run until their emails are sent. Handle errors per reminder and execute each database deletion after its corresponding successful cancellation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks

The async callbacks passed to forEach are discarded, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch failures from the newly asynchronous getCalendar call, including module-loading and CalendarService-construction errors. Previously, synchronous initialization errors reached this catch; now they become unhandled promise rejections while Reschedule proceeds to send email and report success. Await Promise.all over a map, or use an awaited loop, so initialization and cleanup failures are handled. The same change is needed in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

true_positives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
